correctness.rationale: On the specified labels, the bipartite edges A_rB_s for s=r,r−1,r+2 are exactly the two cycle edges at each even vertex and the added even-to-i+5 chord. If a legal force's target stays white as the blue set grows, its source still has only that white neighbor. This justifies parallel closure and monotonicity, so testing all four-sets excludes every smaller size. An independent exhaustive check, not a rerun of the frozen scripts, found zero forcing sets among 495 four-sets and 324 among 792 five-sets. It enumerated all 48 adjacency-preserving permutations and recovered the nine stated orbits with sizes 12,24,24,24,48,48,48,48,48 and the stated representative degrees and eccentricities. The one-replacement graphs and all-source shortest paths gave connected J/T with (edges,radius,diameter)=(2910,5,5)/(534,9,13), slide degree counts 3:276,4:24,6:24, and eccentricity counts 9:24,10:144,11:60,12:48,13:48. Comparing every jump edge against the slide distance matrix gave maximum 9, attained by the stated {0,2,5,6,11} to {0,5,6,9,11} pair; shortest paths rule out any smaller distance for that witness. The excess over the single jump is eight moves. Replay: /workspace/branches/f916f99d-38ec-42cb-a181-5e8c7bd1d5f8/independent_check.py and independent_output.json. The check is exhaustive for this ordinary-forcing graph only.

evidence: A slide is a jump with an additional host adjacency condition. The different examples demonstrate that jump connectivity alone does not force slide connectivity; in particular the Möbius–Kantor ordinary-forcing slide graph is edgeless while its jump graph is connected.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Definitions and the general spanning-subgraph inclusion do not imply connectivity or exact Franklin slide radius, diameter, and per-jump detour, even assuming the ordinary jump graph is connected. Those facts require determining the actual admissible replacements.

value.rationale: The Franklin graph is a canonical small cubic vertex-transitive host, rather than an arbitrary sampled case. Its complete minimum-set geometry is a useful exact benchmark: both move graphs stay connected, yet a single jump can require nine optimal slides and the slide eccentricities vary despite host symmetry. The census and shortest-path witness distinguish unrestricted and local movement in a way neither the scalar Z nor generic graph connectivity can.
